item.title: Chinese vice premier meets executive vice chair of National Committee on U.S.-China Relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 -- Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng met with Evan Greenberg, executive vice chair of the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations (NCUSCR), in Beijing on Monday. He, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said Chinese President Xi Jinping paid a state visit to the United States recently, and the two heads of state agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. China and the United States should jointly implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, and inject more certainty and stability into China-U.S. economic and trade cooperation and the world economy, He said. It is hoped that the NCUSCR will continue to play an active role in promoting China-U.S. economic cooperation, He added. Stressing that stable development of U.S.-China relations is of great significance, the U.S. side expressed willingness to continue to play a bridging role in promoting enhanced economic exchanges and cooperation between the two sides.

item.title: Chinese premier meets Vietnam's National Assembly chairman
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 12 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Tran Thanh Man, chairman of the National Assembly of Vietnam, in Beijing on Monday. Reflecting "camaraderie plus brotherhood," Li said China is willing to work with Vietnam to continue traditional friendship, enhance unity and mutual trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, better benefit the two peoples, and inject positive energy into promoting regional and global stability and prosperity. Li said that China stands ready to enhance alignment of development strategies with the Vietnamese side, expand and optimize the economic and trade pie between the two countries, and continuously improve the quality and efficiency of cooperation in areas such as connectivity, artificial intelligence, clean energy and the digital economy. He called on the two sides to deepen people-to-people exchanges and cooperation in medicine, education, youth and other fields, to cement the public opinion foundation for China-Vietnam friendship. In the face of the complex and volatile international situation, China is ready to enhance communication and collaboration with Vietnam under multilateral frameworks such as APEC, China-ASEAN and the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation to jointly address risks and challenges, he said. Li also expressed the hope that the legislative bodies of the two countries will strongly support the bilateral practical cooperation and play a greater role in providing legal guarantees and promoting people-to-people bonds. Tran Thanh Man said Vietnam extends its heartfelt congratulations on China's new and significant achievements in economic and social development, with its economic growth rate ranking among the top of the world's major economies and its breakthroughs in scientific and technological innovation leading the world. Vietnam has always regarded China as a top priority and a strategic choice in its foreign relations, firmly adheres to the one-China policy, and will maintain close exchanges with China at all levels in accordance with the important consensus reached by the top leaders of the two parties and two countries, Tran Thanh Man added. The National Assembly of Vietnam attaches great importance to and highly recognizes Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, and is willing to enhance exchanges of experience in governance with China, he noted.

item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. He said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said.

item.title: China ready to expand cooperation with New Zealand in services trade, new energy sectors, says premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 -- China is ready to work with New Zealand to tap the potential of trade in services and expand cooperation in sectors such as new energy vehicles, photovoltaics and wind power, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Monday during a phone conversation with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. China-New Zealand relations have maintained steady and sound momentum, with new progress made in cooperation across various fields, Li said. Meanwhile, the international situation remains complex and evolving, with unilateralism and protectionism continuing to weigh on the global economy, he said, adding that calls from the international community to safeguard the multilateral system and strengthen openness and cooperation are growing louder. As supporters and practitioners of multilateralism and free trade, China and New Zealand should strengthen communication and coordination, Li said. Noting that the two countries will mark the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations next year, Li said China stands ready to work with New Zealand to carry forward their traditional friendship, expand mutually beneficial cooperation and deepen their comprehensive strategic partnership, injecting fresh impetus into the stability, development and prosperity in both countries, the region and the world. Li said China is willing to work with New Zealand to remain partners that respect each other and pursue mutual benefit and win-win cooperation. He called on both sides to continue to expand the scale and improve the quality of bilateral trade in goods, tap the potential of trade in services, and expand cooperation in areas such as new energy vehicles, photovoltaics and wind power to deliver more tangible results. The premier expressed hope that the two sides will accelerate negotiations on a negative list for trade in services under the China-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement and achieve substantive progress at an early date. The two countries should facilitate people-to-people exchanges and deepen exchanges and cooperation in culture, tourism, education, young people and sub-national entities to strengthen the foundation of friendship between their peoples, Li said. As members of the Asia-Pacific family, China and New Zealand should also strengthen cooperation within the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) framework and actively advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, he added. For his part, Luxon said New Zealand-China relations are developing steadily, with practical cooperation advancing across various fields and benefiting the peoples of both countries. New Zealand attaches great importance to its relationship with China and remains firmly committed to the one-China policy, he said. New Zealand is willing to take the opportunity of next year's 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations to strengthen high-level exchanges with China, deepen mutual understanding and trust, and enhance practical cooperation in trade, tourism, new energy and other areas to advance the comprehensive strategic partnership, he said. Luxon also expressed New Zealand's support for China's hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. The two sides also exchanged views on international and regional issues of common concern.

item.title: High-frequency data points to China's improving economic momentum in Q3
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
BEIJING, Oct. 11 -- China's economy continued to improve in the third quarter of this year, with new growth drivers gaining momentum, official high-frequency data on consumption, trade and investment showed Sunday. Consumer activity continued to recover, with offline consumption payments up 2.6 percent year on year in the third quarter, accelerating by 0.7 percentage points from the second quarter, according to data released by the State Information Center under the National Development and Reform Commission. In September, offline consumption payments increased 3.1 percent from a year earlier, up 0.5 percentage points from August, marking three consecutive months of growth. The data also showed that the weight carried by cargo ships departing from and arriving at major Chinese ports rose 43.1 percent and 0.3 percent year on year, respectively, in the third quarter. On investment, the issuance of new special-purpose bonds rose 50.2 percent year on year in September, 43.6 percentage points faster than the August level, the data showed. The value of contracts awarded for projects related to new infrastructure, including computing power, data and networks, increased 34.2 percent year on year in the third quarter and 50.4 percent year on year last month. Capital investment in frontier sectors such as artificial intelligence and humanoid robots surged 184.1 percent year on year in the third quarter and 198.7 percent year on year in September, the data showed. "Investment in frontier fields such as artificial intelligence has remained strong, supporting current growth while building momentum for the development of new quality productive forces," said Wei Ying, deputy director of the center's big data development department. China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for even better results in practice. In the first half of the year, the country's gross domestic product grew 4.7 percent year on year. In another sign of a firming economy, China's manufacturing activity returned to expansionary territory in September, while non-manufacturing activity rebounded markedly. The purchasing managers' index for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 last month, while the business activity index for the non-manufacturing sector reached 50.2.

item.title: China issues guidelines on developing new quality productive forces
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 9 -- The Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council have issued a set of guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces to bolster high-quality development. These guidelines outline 19 key measures in five areas, namely advancing scientific and technological innovation, deepening the integration of sci-tech and industrial innovation, innovating development approaches, promoting institutional and mechanism innovation, and improving mechanisms for talent development. Noting that developing new quality productive forces is an intrinsic requirement and an important focus of promoting high-quality development, these guidelines stress the importance of innovation-driven development, reform and measures tailored to local conditions, and following the approach of "establishing the new before abolishing the old." The guidelines call for pursuing high technology, high efficiency and high quality, properly handling the relationships between the government and the market, between the qualitative nature of productive forces and the forms they take in industry and business, between reform and development, and between self-reliance and opening up, while coordinating development and security. "The new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation has opened up broad prospects for developing new quality productive forces. Seizing this historic opportunity requires moving faster to achieve greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology and raising innovation capacity across the board to maintain strategic initiative," said Wang Shengxiao, a researcher with the Party School of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. The guidelines call for stronger original and transformative sci-tech innovation, with major sci-tech projects to focus on strategic, landmark and leading products, targeting the cutting-edge of global science and technology and serving major areas of economic development, major national needs, and people's health. They stress the need for faster breakthroughs in key core technologies, including efforts to promote the high-quality development of key manufacturing industrial chains and implement industrial innovation projects in priority areas. The guidelines emphasize coordinated efforts to strengthen national strategic sci-tech capabilities, giving full play to national laboratories in organizing major national sci-tech projects and building major innovation platforms. The guidelines also urge optimizing the roles and distribution of national sci-tech research institutions, high-level research universities and leading sci-tech enterprises. The guidelines underline the principal role of enterprises in sci-tech innovation, encouraging technology-based small and medium-sized enterprises to increase research and development investment and supporting capable private enterprises in taking the lead in major national technological breakthrough tasks. To speed up the transformation of sci-tech achievements into real productive forces, the guidelines call for leveraging the advantages of China's vast market to better connect technology with the market and advance the development of new quality productive forces on a larger scale. The guidelines also urge upgrading traditional industries through the application of digital, intelligent and green technologies. The country should seek to advance producer services toward greater specialization and the higher end of the value chain, while improving the quality, diversity and convenience of consumer services, according to the guidelines. For emerging industries, the guidelines emphasize efforts to foster their growth and develop new pillar industries. The guidelines encourage greater cross-industry and cross-regional integration, measures to avoid "involution-style" competition, and support eastern regions to help central, western and northeastern regions develop emerging industries in line with local conditions. The guidelines call for forward-looking planning for future industries and emphasize the need to make full use of existing fiscal policies to support their development and guide social capital to steadily increase investment. The guidelines also urge promoting the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, optimizing the layout, construction and operation of national data infrastructure, advancing the digital transformation of the manufacturing sector, and building digital industrial clusters with international competitiveness. The guidelines call for fully implementing the "AI Plus" initiative, using artificial intelligence (AI) to transform traditional industries, accelerating innovation in AI and other digital and intelligent technologies, and promoting the widespread application of AI across industries. Efforts are also needed to establish systems for technology monitoring, early risk warning and emergency response to ensure that AI is safe, reliable and controllable, the guidelines note. These guidelines further propose building a green, low-carbon and circular economic system by strengthening green manufacturing, developing green services, expanding the green energy industry, and driving the supply of green products via green consumption. Efforts should be made to optimize the policy toolbox for green development and implement fiscal, financial, investment, pricing, technological and environmental policies that promote green and low-carbon development, according to the guidelines. The country will actively advance the energy revolution and accelerate the green transition of energy use in production and daily life across society, the guidelines add. The guidelines call for deepening reform to promote close integration of science and technology with the economy, saying that efforts should be made to build an open, shared and secure nationally integrated data market. The guidelines also stress the need to improve the market regulation system and increase the supply of innovative financial products. The guidelines pledge to allocate advanced production factors globally by expanding high-standard opening up and actively building a global innovation cooperation network, and encouraging foreign venture capital institutions, international standards organizations and others to develop in China. The guidelines urge cultivating talent urgently needed for the development of new quality productive forces, adding that policies on the use and flow of talent should be improved. "New quality productive forces are primarily driven by transformational technological breakthroughs, which bring profound changes to how innovation is organized, industries evolve and resources are allocated," said Liu Zhenzhong, a researcher at the Institute of Industrial and Technological Economics of the National Development and Reform Commission. "These changes require deeper reforms to reshape institutional frameworks and remove obstacles to development." The outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) identifies the development of new quality productive forces as a key strategic task and sets out 28 major projects related to this goal, accounting for 25.7 percent of the 109 major projects outlined in the plan. The projects focus on four priorities: strengthening industrial capabilities and competitiveness, fostering emerging industries, pursuing breakthroughs in cutting-edge technologies, and enhancing innovation capabilities. At an international seminar held in Beijing in September, Chinese experts said China's development of new quality productive forces could provide fresh momentum for global economic growth and create new opportunities for countries at different stages of modernization. Abdulrahman Bello Dambazau, Nigeria's ambassador to China, noted that the emphasis on talent development, scientific research and industrial upgrading could offer useful reference for developing countries. China's development of high-tech, green and intelligent industries is also creating more opportunities for cross-border investment and industrial cooperation. At the China International Fair for Investment and Trade in September, representatives from European countries explored cooperation with China in areas such as clean energy, AI, smart manufacturing, biomedicine and the digital economy.

item.title: China issues revised regulations on implementation of audit law
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the implementation of the audit law. The revised regulations, which consist of 7 chapters and 64 articles, will take effect on Dec. 1. Highlighting the need to refine and improve audit supervision, the regulations specify the scope and content of audits over fiscal revenues and expenditures, and bring the management and use of state-owned resources into the scope of special audit investigations, among others. To ensure that audit work is free from interference, the regulations add provisions on a registration and reporting system for any unwarranted attempts to inquire about or interfere with audit matters. All departments of the State Council and local authorities at all levels shall strengthen overall coordination, oversee rectification of problems uncovered in audits, and establish and improve relevant systems.
